llm.summary: The skill largely matches its marketing purpose, but several incoherent or risky choices (embedded API keys, mismatched network allowlist vs runtime hosts, and references to other skills' paths / local system services) warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (social media analysis, titles/scripts, product/author analysis) aligns with the code and shipped data. However, the repository already contains concrete API credentials in scripts/config.js (TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY) which is unnecessary for publishing the skill and inconsistent with the manifest’s 'doNotCommitToVcs' guidance. Also scripts/cmd_vid_integration.py references a specific path to another local skill (~/.openclaw-agent2/.../chanjing-one-click-video-creation), which is not obviously required by the stated high-level README instructions and assumes/attempts to interact with other local agent components.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md tells users to git clone and run node marketing_hub.js config <TikHubToken> <DeepSeekKey> — reasonable. But runtime code goes beyond: it spawns child processes (curl, chrome, Xvfb), attempts to run a local Chrome binary (/usr/bin/google-chrome), may start Xvfb, and the python integration expects/attempts to invoke another skill's run_render.py under the user's home. The manifest lists only api.tikhub.io and api.deepseek.com as allowed/documented hosts, yet the code scrapes https://www.douyin.com and runs browser automation against it — a mismatch between declared scope and actual network access. The code also writes to scripts/memory and other files in the skill directory (expected) but also touches or expects other paths in the user's home (~/.openclaw-agent2), which is out-of-band relative to the SKILL.md instructions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No installer; instruction-only install (git clone) and Node scripts — low install risk. There is no packaged download from an arbitrary URL. However, the repository includes executable scripts that will run system commands when invoked.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The manifest declares no required env vars, but runtime behavior requires two API credentials (TikHub and DeepSeek). SKILL.md instructs users to provide them via node marketing_hub.js config. Despite this, a scripts/config.js file in the repo already contains concrete-looking tokens (including a 'sk-...' style key). That is an incoherence (secrets committed in tree while manifest says they shouldn't be). The embedded keys may be real or leaked; either way, shipping keys in code is a proportionality and secrets-exposure concern. The skill does not request unrelated cloud credentials, but it does perform local OS interactions (starting Xvfb, executing Chrome) that may require elevated capabilities on some systems.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no global skill modifications — appropriate. The skill writes into its own scripts/memory directory (declared in manifest). Concern: a shipped Python helper references and attempts to call a script in ~/.openclaw-agent2/workspace-collector/skills/... which would access other skills and user home directories; this is privilege/footprint creep beyond its declared read/write roots and could cross skill boundaries unexpectedly.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Key points to consider before installing or running this skill:

- Embedded API keys: scripts/config.js contains hardcoded TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY values. Do NOT assume these are safe to use — they may be leaked or abused. Replace them with your own keys, and remove or rotate any keys you find in committed files. The manifest even listed config.js in doNotCommitToVcs, yet the file was committed — that's a red flag about the maintainer's handling of secrets.

- Network / allowlist mismatch: The manifest only documents api.tikhub.io and api.deepseek.com, but the code scrapes https://www.douyin.com and uses external browser automation. Verify network policies/allowlists in your environment before running, and be prepared that scraping may contact additional hosts.

- Local system interactions: The Node scripts will spawn processes (curl, chrome, Xvfb) and may start/kill Xvfb or run Chrome with flags. Running these requires system binaries and can affect running services. Review the code paths that call exec/execSync (marketing_hub.js and cmd_vid_integration.py) to ensure no user-input is passed unsafely into shell commands in your usage scenario.

- Cross-skill / home-directory access: cmd_vid_integration.py references a fixed path under your home (~/.openclaw-agent2/...), attempting to call another skill's run_render.py. That reads other skills and assumes a particular environment layout. If you don't have or trust that other local skill, disable or audit this integration.

- Audit before running: Look for and remove any hardcoded secrets, run the scripts in a sandbox or controlled environment, and consider running with network restrictions (or reviewing and adding any additional hosts to an allowlist you control). If you need the functionality, prefer configuring the API keys yourself (via the provided config command) and verify that the DeepSeek key is your own and not the one in config.js.

- If unsure: classify this as potentially risky and avoid granting it broad network or filesystem privileges (especially running as an elevated user). If you choose to run, do so in an isolated environment and rotate any keys that were exposed in the repository.
